title: The building of Malchus: from a point to a whole face
overview: Chapter 48 of *Shaar HaYichud* continues the study of *Malchus*, the end of all the levels. It explains how *Malchus* is built up from a single point into a complete *partzuf* of all ten *sefiros*, and how that is renewed. On *Rosh Hashanah* and the ten days of *teshuvah* the *Keser* of the *Nukva* is built, and the ten *pesukim* of *Malchiyos* reveal the source of *Malchus* in the *Torah*. Its essence is *hisnasus*, the transcendence that rises above and so reveals G-d in something separate. *Hisnasus* needs something outside itself: a king needs a people, and his leadership is made by their *bittul*. This is why the *sefiros* are a projection from us: a mirror in which we see ourselves, and G-d relates to us as we are. The first *tzimtzum*, the empty place, was made so that there would be something outside the essence where *hisnasus* could show. The curtain between *Atzilus* and *Beriya* lets the *Malchus* of *Atzilus* come down as the head of the foxes. The chapter ends with *ani rishon* and *ani acharon*: the beginning of *Malchus* is rooted in its end, which is why it is renewed every year.

sections.title: Malchus is built from a point into a whole face of the sefiros
sections.summary: The kingship of the Ein Sof is revealed in speech and in everything. Malchus is the end of all the levels, and it is built up through the whole descent.

phrases.en: the details of the *binyan* of *Malchus*
a complete *partzuf* of all ten *sefiros*

phrases.he: היינו מה שבבחינת הדבור מתגלה הכל
phrases.en: the metaphor for this is how everything, a person's thoughts, their intellect, their emotions, everything gets expressed in speech
like the words of speech
that reveal everything

blocks.text: This class goes into the details of the *binyan* of *Malchus*, the building of kingship. *Malchus* starts as a point and is built into a complete *partzuf* (face) of all ten *sefiros*.
The metaphor is speech: thoughts, intellect and emotions are revealed in words, and once a person has labels for everything he can express them in a tangible way.

Naming something makes it more of a *yesh*, a concrete thing. A patient with a skin rash hears 'you have cellulitis', which just means a skin rash in Latin. The name sometimes helps and sometimes gets in the way.
blocks.title: A rash with a Latin name

blocks.text: Words let an idea be expressed to someone else as something separate. Once it is said it cannot be taken back, and it becomes separate from the person who said it.

phrases.he: והוא גם מבחינת התענוג ורצון העצמי שבעצמות אור אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: even to the essential *ratzon* and *taanug*, or the essential *taanug* and *ratzon*, in the essence of the *Ein Sof*
which was that *chafetz chesed*

phrases.he: כשבא בהשתלשלות רבות עד רצון וחכמה ומדות דאדם קדמון
phrases.en: that comes down through many, a whole process of *hishtalshelus*, until it comes into the *ratzon* and *chachma* and *middos* of *Adam Kadmon*
and then *Arich Anpin*, it goes from *Adam Kadmon* to the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, which is called *Arich Anpin*

phrases.he: עד בחינת רצון וחכמה ומדות חיצוניות הכלים דזעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: until the way that the *ratzon* and *chachma* and *middos* are expressed in the external vessels of the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*
so all of this is expressed in through *Malchus*
the idea of the supernal speech, G-d's speech
reveals everything as a tangible thing
about this it says
I am first and I am last, and the *ani* is *Malchus*

phrases.he: וכן ראו כי אני אני הוא,
phrases.en: and similarly it says see that I, I am he

phrases.he: בחינת מלכות דאין סוף במלכות דאצילות,
phrases.en: In other words, that *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* is really being revealed directly in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*
the end of all levels

blocks.text: This holds at every level of the chain of descent: the essential *ratzon* and *taanug* of the *Ein Sof* is the *chafetz chesed*.
G-d can create something from nothing. He can reveal it as a separate thing, so creation seems independent of Him. That is the power of *Malchus*.

The *chafetz chesed* comes down through many levels of *hishtalshelus* until the *ratzon*, *chachma* and *middos* of *Adam Kadmon*, then *Arich Anpin*, which reaches the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, and then the external *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*. In a person it is like desires felt in the body, a change in heart rate or breathing.

All of this is expressed through *Malchus*, the supernal speech of G-d, which reveals everything as a tangible thing in *Atzilus*. The *Malchus* of *Atzilus* that goes down is a topic he will come back to.

'I am first and I am last' is *Malchus*. *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* is G-d's essential ability to reveal Himself in any form, and its inner nature is *hisnasus*, transcending all limits, so He can reveal even the infinite as something finite.

The revelation of *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* shows up in our *mesiras nefesh* for *Torah* and *mitzvos*: a compulsion that feels like our own. But we are literally a piece of G-d (*chelek Elokah*), and that is where it comes from.

*Malchus* is at every level, from the *Ein Sof* down through *Adam Kadmon*, *Keser* and *Arich Anpin* to the *Malchus* that reveals *Zeir Anpin*. The 'I' at the top and the 'I' at the bottom are the same, and the 'he' is the concealment before the *tzimtzum*.

*Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* is revealed directly in *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the end of all levels. This is the concept to explain: how *Malchus* reveals everything on every level, the *binyan* of *Malchus*.

sections.title: Rosh Hashanah rebuilds Malchus: the Keser of the Nukva and the ten pesukim of Malchiyos
sections.summary: On Rosh Hashanah and the ten days of teshuvah we build Malchus again, awakening G-d's desire to be king and our own acceptance of it.

phrases.en: but first we have to understand
in a detailed way
about the *partzuf* of *Malchus*
from the *Keser* of it
all the way to the *Malchus*
is what splits the curtain
and it becomes the *Keser* of *Beriya*

phrases.he: דהנה בראש השנה הוא בנין כתר הנוקבא
phrases.en: so on *Rosh Hashanah* we build the *Keser* of *Malchus*

phrases.he: כו', והוא מה שאומרים י' פסוקים מלכיות כו'
phrases.en: and this is why we say the 10 *pesukim* of *Malchiyos*

blocks.text: In the particular way (*derech prat*), the *partzuf* of *Malchus* has all ten *sefiros*, from its *Keser* down to *Malchus*.
The last *Malchus*, the *Malchus* of the *partzuf* of *Malchus*, splits the curtain between *Atzilus* and *Beriya* and becomes the *Keser* of *Beriya*.

Each of the ten days of *teshuvah* builds one *sefira* of *Malchus*, starting with the *Keser* of the *Nukva* on *Rosh Hashanah*. *Rosh Hashanah* also builds *Malchus* to a degree, which is creating the *Keser* of the *Nukva*.
We say the ten *pesukim* of *Malchiyos* to reveal the source of *Malchus* in the *Torah*.

We awaken the desire for *Malchus*, as it were, in G-d's own desire to be king, and in ourselves by accepting *kabbalas ol malchus shamayim*. That creates a new *ratzon* to fulfill what He says, and reveals the *mesiras nefesh* we have.

phrases.he: דהיינו להמשיך בחינת התענוג והרצון למלוכה מחדש,
phrases.en: the idea that on *Rosh Hashanah* we want to renew the pleasure and desire for kingship

phrases.he: שהוא לעורר מחדש בחינת התענוג והרצון הפשוט שבעצמות,
phrases.en: all the way up to the *taanug* and *ratzon pashut* in the *Atzmus*
before the *tzimtzum*, in order that he should have the desire of *ana emloch*, to say that I'm going to be king

phrases.he: כו' (והיינו ענין גבורי כח עושי דברו
phrases.en: this is what it says is that the mighty, the people with might, they, the simple meaning is they do his words
like it explains in the *Zohar*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ויתנו לך כתר מלוכה כו')
phrases.en: that we give the crown of kingship to Hashem

blocks.text: On *Rosh Hashanah* we renew the pleasure and desire for kingship, reaching up to the simple *taanug* and *ratzon* in the *Atzmus*, before the *tzimtzum*, so that G-d has the desire of *ana emloch*, 'I'm going to be king', as we talked about back in chapter 10.
The simple meaning of *gibborei koach*, 'who do His word', is that even the mightiest do what G-d says. Here it is read as: we make His words.

Through our *mesiras nefesh* and commitment on *Rosh Hashanah* we create the *ratzon* and *taanug* in these things. That is the point of the *Zohar*, and of the verse about giving Hashem the crown of kingship.

sections.title: Hisnasus is the essence of Malchus, and it needs something outside itself
sections.summary: Hisnasus, rising above, is the middah of Malchus. It is awakened only in relation to others; kindness, by contrast, comes from the essence.

phrases.he: בהיות ידוע שבחינת ההתגלות בדבור הנזכר לעיל, הוא הנקרא דבר מלך,
phrases.en: being that it's known, that when G-d is revealed in speech this is called the word of the king
externally *Malchus* is the idea of *dibur*, of just revealing something, but in its essence it is the *middah* of *hisnasus*, of transcendence

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב יהו״ה מלך גאות כו'
phrases.en: like it says, that Hashem is king and he garbs himself in *gaos*
and similarly we say that Your kingship is a *Malchus* of all worlds

blocks.text: The revelation in *dibur* is called the word of the king, *dvar melech*. Externally *Malchus* is *dibur*; in its essence it is *hisnasus*, transcendence.

*Malchus* expresses G-d's essence. Because G-d transcends all limits, He reveals Himself in something separate, a *yesh*. Why we awaken this *ratzon*, Rabbi Walters thinks, is that communication is collaborative.
People crown a king, and that creates in him a desire to rule them when he sees they are *batel* and ready to listen. In them it creates a *ratzon* and *taanug* to follow him.
blocks.title: Crowning a king

blocks.text: Language works the same way. Words are meaningless until people agree to give them meaning, and then they have power, like a contract. Attach *ratzon* and *taanug* to them and they become very powerful.

So G-d's ability to be king in the world comes from our commitment to follow Him and to do *Torah* and *mitzvos*. These express the connection and reveal the *yechida*, though to a degree it depends on our accepting them.
'Hashem is king, He garbs Himself in *gaos*.' *Gaos* is usually translated as arrogance, but here it means being exalted over others, in a positive sense.

A king has to withdraw himself. A teacher makes rules for a classroom to put the burden of effort on the students, with points and tests, and then removes himself from them as if he had no choice, though he does. By making himself aloof he creates the reality that forces them to work and allows them to develop.
blocks.title: The classroom rules

blocks.text: In a similar way G-d made time, space and nature seem a fixed reality, which gives us a sense of reality and makes us work within it. *Torah* and *mitzvos* are a further layer for revealing G-dliness. A listener's example, that a good business runs on systems, is taken up: you set up systems so you don't have to do it.
The *Rebbe* describes a factory that runs by itself, with no people. That shows how fully the designer put his wisdom into it: the revelation of G-dliness in nature itself.
blocks.title: The automated factory

blocks.text: Some revelation is purely within nature. Another, the *reshimu*, reveals the infinite within creation by its own nature. *Tzimtzum* removes His infinite choice, yet what He made still has infinite wisdom and power.

*Kav* is progressive growth, as in *Torah* and *mitzvos*; a miracle goes beyond all that. Each is a unique revelation of G-d's infinity, *yachid*, *echad* and *kadmon*, and that is why there are all three.
*Malchus* comes through on every level of 'Your kingship of all worlds', through all those limitations. Who says why gravity? It is just because Hashem said so.
The limitations, the ten *sefiros*, why *chesed* is opposite *gevura*, and their order, all come from Hashem's *Malchus*, which is a direct revelation and choice from His *Atzmus*.

phrases.en: for example, by way of analogy
the idea of leadership in a person

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מדה נבדלת מן העצמות,
phrases.en: that this is something that's like the ability, the *middah* of being able to connect to something that's separate from yourself
it's the idea that you're going to put yourself in a position of superiority and leadership on top of others

phrases.he: כו', מה שאין כן שאר המדות שהן חלק ממש מן העצמות
phrases.en: in contrast all the other *middos*, they're all like part of the self

blocks.text: For example, take *hisnasus* in a person: a *middah* separate from the essence, the ability to connect to something separate from oneself, to be above others. It is not negative superiority; it means being assertive and acting aloof in a positive way, as a leader.

The other *middos* are a direct self-expression and need nothing else. Curiosity and kindness relate to the self, though kindness also reaches another. Leadership depends on other people, as does communication.

phrases.en: for example, the light of *kindness*
that the soul itself, the person himself has this innate desire to do kindness

phrases.he: כי עיקר מדה זו המשכה מן העצמות הוא,
phrases.en: cuz the main idea of *chesed* is that you have this innate quality that you want to be kind

phrases.he: כמו כן החכמה נמשכת מן העצם כו'
phrases.en: So too wisdom is coming from the person's essence

blocks.text: For example, the light of *chesed*: the soul itself is drawn to kindness, because this *middah* comes from the essence, an expression of something unique within a person. So too *chachma* is drawn from the essence: we have an innate desire to find patterns, an intuition and a curiosity.

phrases.he: אבל מדת ההתנשאות, הגם שהנפש מתפעלת ממנה,
phrases.en: but in contrast this *middah* of leadership, even though the person does get affected by it

phrases.he: אבל העיקר שלה הוא המתהווה מן הדבר הנבדל מן העצם,
phrases.en: but it's mainly created by the outside, things that are outside of you, by the circumstances you're in
which is the fact that you're with the other person

phrases.he: ואם אין דבר זולתו לא תתעורר מדה זו כלל
phrases.en: if you don't have something else, it doesn't awaken, you don't get this desire to, you know, rule over somebody or dominate them or communicate with them, it's not awakened at all

blocks.text: *Hisnasus* is different: even though the soul is affected by it, its main source is outside, in things outside you and in the circumstances you are in, the fact that you are with another person. If there is nothing else, this *middah* does not awaken at all, like wanting to overcome a challenge.

phrases.he: והגם שבחינת החסד גם כן להטיב חסדו לזולתו דוקא, אבל מכל מקום תחלת התהוותה הוא בעצמותו, גם שאין איש להטיב עמו,

phrases.en: It comes from the other thing, the thing that's outside of us

phrases.he: שלא תתהווה בעצם מציאותה בלתי מי שיש להתנשאות עליו
phrases.en: the main *mashal* is like a king, or any sort of a leadership, when you're in a group with a bunch of people, and they want you to lead them

blocks.text: *Chesed* also reaches others, but it starts in the essence; *hisnasus* starts with the other. The main *mashal* is a king: when people want you to lead them, it makes you take the position, but a person on his own does not have it the same way.
blocks.title: The leader of a group

blocks.text: Rabbi Walters thinks every person has an innate wish to dominate things: animals, language, art, bending things to one's will. But it comes mostly from what is outside us; a puzzle makes a person want to solve it. Every *middah* has an inside and an outside aspect.

Earlier we spoke of *ratzon kadum*, a desire not from the outside world, plugged into the *ratzon* of *Adam Kadmon* as a revealing of what is hidden (*gilui ha'helem*). That is *Malchus*: we have innate things inside and want to imprint them on what is outside us.

*Chesed* seems to need someone else, to do kindness to another, but as the *maamar* says at its start, it is originally in the self, even if there is nobody to do kindness to. Leadership or dominance does not exist in a person until there is someone to rule over.

phrases.he: וראיה לזה ממה שכל עיקר בנינה בהתפשטות אורך ורוחב תלוי רק בביטול האנשים,
phrases.en: the main thing that builds up and causes the development and the expression of this to the length and the width is only from
when they exalt him and they hold him in high esteem and they look to him for leadership, then that awakens in him this feeling of exaltedness and leadership

phrases.he: ובמיעוט הביטול ימעיטו אור מדה זו כו'
phrases.en: and if people don't want to listen to him, then it diminishes this

blocks.text: The proof: the length and breadth of this *middah* depend only on the *bittul* of people. When people exalt a leader and look to him, it awakens in him the feeling of *hisnasus*; if they don't want to listen, it diminishes this *middah*.

phrases.he: אבל החסד כמו שהוא בעצם כך יתפשט,
phrases.en: but *chesed* is different
even though it can also be sometimes more or less, if the person, you know, awakens the person's kindness

phrases.he: על פי אופן התעוררות המקבל אם הוא מבקש ברחמנות ביותר
phrases.en: if a person really asks with pleas for mercy, so then it's going to awaken the person's kindness

phrases.he: כו', מכל מקום לא מזה יבא עיקר בנינה כו' ודי למבין.
phrases.en: but that's not really where it's coming from. It was already in the person

blocks.text: *Chesed* is different: it is in a person as in the essence, and it does not depend on another. It can be more or less depending how the recipient awakens it; if someone pleads for mercy, that awakens the kindness. But that is not where it comes from; it was already in the person.
There are two parts of ourselves: the innate character we express, and the ability to relate to what is outside of us.

Rabbi Walters thinks anyone who is put in a leadership position knows it: when people depend on you and ask you, you rise to the occasion and develop a desire to take care of everyone. But again, it is created from the situation.
blocks.title: Put in charge

sections.title: A king needs a people: Malchus is where G-d relates to our perspective
sections.summary: A king is made by the bittul of the people. The ten sefiros are a projection from us, the way a mirror shows us ourselves.

phrases.en: and the *nimshal* for this is, we have to understand, what is the *nimshal* above

phrases.he: כי כמו מלכותא דארעא כך מלכותא דרקיע,
phrases.en: that the kingship on Earth is similar to the kingship of Heaven
that just like in a physical king, a person can only be a king if he has a people

blocks.text: The *nimshal* is that earthly kingship is like the kingship of Heaven: a king can only be a king if he has a people, just as in a physical kingdom.
blocks.title: A king needs a people

blocks.text: When people love and praise a leader and believe in him, it makes him a different type of person. This happens even with celebrities, and with a political leader when everybody is cheering for him.

phrases.he: והגם שההתנשאות דבחינת מדת מלכות למעלה
phrases.en: even though this *hisnasus* of the *middah* of *Malchus* above is like all the other *sefiros*

phrases.he: הוא כשאר המדות העליונות, אבל אינה המשכה ממש מבחינת העצמות
phrases.en: but still it's not quite the same

blocks.text: *Hisnasus* of *Malchus* above is like the other higher *middos*, one of the ten *sefiros*. Without people, a person is not a king.

It is not quite the same: it does not flow directly from the *Atzmus*. The other nine *sefiros* are objective reality. *Malchus* is where G-d creates us with our subjective perspective, and He relates to us as we are.

It depends on us. Rabbi Walters thinks this is related: our models, like a language, are a convention; they convey something of reality but are not reality itself. G-d created our ability to relate to Him this way.
When we project our human needs onto G-d, He relates to us that way, the way a king, when people say 'we need you', is awakened to want to be their king.
blocks.title: The king people need

blocks.text: How can *bittul* and kingship be one *middah*? They seem opposite: one is listening, the other is telling everyone what to do. True kingship is not tyranny. The people ask the king to lead, and he takes on the role of a servant leader, subjugating himself to serve them. In Hebrew, a *melech* and a *moshel* are different.
It is a great *bittul* for the king too: he dedicates his life to his people and loses his private identity. You see this with the *Rebbeim*, whose everything belongs to the *chassidim*.
People must have *bittul* to the king for him to be king, and the king must have the corresponding *bittul*, so the relationship works both ways. The *bittul* also has an aspect of *hisnasus*.
Deferring to what you are told and doing your duty, like a soldier, shows you can transcend yourself. So the real essence of *Malchus* is the power of transcendence.
Either way, you give up your identity: to serve, or to lead and use all your abilities for the cause. That is the real essence of *Malchus*, *hisnasus*.

The other *sefiros* are a nature G-d reveals for Himself, a kind of limitation. *Malchus* comes from *hisnasus*, higher than the others, since it transcends limits and so can be revealed in other things. A deep *maamar* on this, about Moshe going up to *marom*, says G-d mirrors us face to face; the *sefiros* are a projection from us.
A parent making rules for a child must put himself aside and understand the child's potential; the rules are a projection of the child, mirrored and enlarged.
blocks.title: The parent's rules

blocks.text: By the child accepting that and giving *bittul*, he develops into it. In a similar way a leader sees the potential of the country and its people, becomes its representation, and brings it out to the people.
Language works the same way: a thing that is *batel*, like water that reflects things. It has no meaning on its own, and you project meaning into it, and the words can guide you and pick you up.

You project yourself outward in rules and structures that come from inside, and they anchor you to the parts of yourself you don't always have the strength to bring out. A commitment does this: externalized, it pulls you up.
Many *midrashim* say our whole concept of G-d is a projection from us. G-d's essence is a transcendent reality, and because it is simple it can reflect anything, including us.
Look in a mirror, or at water, and you see your reflection. The face you see comes from you, not the mirror, yet the fact that it reflects you is the revelation of the mirror itself.
blocks.title: The mirror

blocks.text: How do you know you are looking at a mirror? You see yourself in it. The projection comes from you, but it is also the revelation of the mirror. We view the *sefiros* through our human lens; with the right *bittul* we project ourselves there, and G-d created us with ten *koachos* and a subjective reality.
Like an author or filmmaker who creates an illusion for the audience, G-d understands what we will perceive and intentionally creates an experience for us.
blocks.title: The movie director

blocks.text: *Malchus* is G-d's ability to know our perspective and create it. It is our subjective reality, not objective like the other *sefiros*, and in a sense it is separate from Him. Our subjectivity is important, since G-d created it, and everything we experience comes through it.

*Malchus* above, like the other higher *middos*, is not a flow from the *Atzmus*: G-d relates to our perception of Him and of reality. Our perception is not reality itself; it is just how we see it, and it is flawed.

phrases.en: but nevertheless there is
This *middah* of *Malchus* exists in the *etzem*, in the potential, in a very hidden way.
like we see in a person
even a small child
They have this attribute of *hisnasus*
they want to dominate everything
even an animal
This is a natural thing in a person
and G-d said when he created man that you should subdue and rule over all the animals

blocks.text: But nevertheless *hisnasus* exists in potential and in great concealment. In a person, even a small child has the attribute of *hisnasus*.
A child wants to dominate everything, even animals; this is natural in a person, as the verse says, to subdue and rule over the animals.

phrases.en: we see the nature of a child

phrases.he: שתשוקתו למשול ולרדות על חיה ובהמה ועוף כו',
phrases.en: that they want to rule over and control animals and birds and everything
as explained elsewhere
and this is the nature of a person

phrases.he: מה שאין כן מדת החסד והרחמים שישנה בבהמה גם כן, כנשר שהוא רחמני כו')
phrases.en: In contrast, the *middah* of *chesed* and *rachamim* and these other kind of *middos* you have also in animals, like it says that an eagle is merciful

blocks.text: We see the nature of a child: they want to rule over and control animals, birds and everything, a trait specifically human. We want to bend everything to our will, making tools and language and domesticating animals. *Chesed* and *rachamim* are also in animals; an eagle is merciful.

This is a uniquely human thing, which is why we are called speakers: we can externalize things. Language lets us store information outside us, so we can build something bigger than ourselves. We make machines that take our understanding and become more powerful than us.

Whenever we meet a situation we want to master it, control it and turn it into a tool. Corn and wheat were once grasses with tiny seeds that we domesticated. Cauliflower, broccoli and Brussels sprouts all come from wild mustard, selectively bred for different traits.
blocks.title: From wild mustard

blocks.text: We envision how we can see ourselves in things outside us and how to use them. In a similar way all the G-dly *koachos* are revealed in us.
How G-dly *koachos* appear in us is not essential; it depends on how we work and on our history, like *Pesach*. Yet the complete revelation of the *Ein Sof* can be found in these things.
So it goes both ways: G-dliness is reflected in us, and G-d can reflect us. We are separate in a way, yet these infinite things can be revealed within us.

phrases.en: even though *Malchus* is called the *middah* of *hisnasus*, of leadership or being exalted, transcending

phrases.he: אבל עיקר בנינה הוא להתנשאות על דרך זולתו,
phrases.en: but nevertheless, it's mainly becomes built up, its whole form comes from something outside

phrases.he: ואז נמשך תענוג ורצון גדול בהתנשאות זו,
phrases.en: And then a person gets a great pleasure and there's a big desire from this *hisnasus*, from this mastery and dominance of the thing that's outside of you

phrases.he: ולפי זה יש להבין איך יתכן למעלה באלקות, שאין לך דבר חוץ ממנו על מי יתנשא
phrases.en: based on this we can understand how we can explain this idea of *Malchus* in G-dliness, because even though really there's nothing separate from G-d, so who can he be ruling over
so it's not like a king that has, like you said, you can only be a king if you have separate people, and you say, I want to rule over them, but G-d, there's only him

blocks.text: Even though *Malchus* is called the *middah* of *hisnasus*, its main building is to be exalted over something other than oneself, and then great pleasure and desire come from this *hisnasus*. Its whole form comes from something outside, unlike an internal sense of what it means to be kind.

Other *middos* are innate, and their expression depends on circumstances while their character does not. Rabbi Walters thinks people enjoy watching others climb mountains and do feats, physical or intellectual; they look for challenges to accomplish things.
The desire is built on the thing outside you, like playing a game or solving a puzzle. A person gets great pleasure and a big desire from this mastery and dominance of what is outside you.
Based on this, how can *Malchus* exist in G-dliness? There is nothing outside Him, so over whom does He rule? Unlike a king who needs separate people, there is only Him, and He creates us.

sections.title: Malchus starts as a point, and the first tzimtzum makes room for it
sections.summary: Malchus cannot be built right away, since it needs something separate. The first tzimtzum, the empty place, makes that separateness.

phrases.he: ואם כן בחינת בנין המלכות ברצון ותענוג ומדות בבחינת פרצוף שלם בבחינת האצילות אי אפשר להיות,
phrases.en: And so therefore you can't have this idea of, unlike the other *partzufim* in *Atzilus* which can be built right away, *Malchus* isn't built right away

phrases.he: כי אם כאשר עלה ברצונו שיהיה יש נפרד לעצמו,
phrases.en: it starts off as just a point, because you can only build *Malchus* once you have something that's separate

once there's a desire to create something that's separate beings, create souls and angels and all these separate creatures, so then there could be a desire to dominate those things, to be the king over those things

phrases.he: כו', אזי נתעורר אור מדה זו מן המאציל כו'
phrases.en: then this light becomes awakened from the *ma'atzil*

blocks.text: So *Malchus* cannot be built right away like the other *partzufim* in *Atzilus*; it starts as a point, because it needs something separate.
Once He desires separate beings, souls, angels and creatures, there can be a desire to dominate them as king. Then this light of the *middah* is awakened from the *ma'atzil* (the Emanator).

phrases.he: ולזאת אמר יהו״ה מלך גאות לבש, שנתלבש במדה זו להיות מלך על עם
phrases.en: and therefore we say that Hashem is king and he dresses himself in *gaos*, that he puts it on like a garment, to be the king over people

blocks.text: Therefore Hashem is king and dresses Himself in *gaos*, putting on this *middah* like a garment, to be king over the people. The garment depends on the separate creatures.

phrases.he: ועל כן צריך דוקא למדה זאת לחדש אותה ממקור חוצבה בכל ראש השנה,
phrases.en: and that's why we need to reawaken this *middah* from new from its source, every *Rosh Hashanah*

phrases.he: דהיינו עד בחינת מחשבה בעצמות אור אין סוף, אנא אמלוך כו',
phrases.en: we have to go all the way up back to the beginning of the whole *seder hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: בבחינת ההתנשאות שעלה בבחינת עצמותו עדיין קודם שהיה הצמצום כו'
phrases.en: and this is the idea that we have to go all the way back to this *hisnasus* that's in His essence, before the *tzimtzum*

blocks.text: So we must renew this *middah* from its source every *Rosh Hashanah*, since we don't know what the *middah* of *Malchus* will be until we know the people's situation.

Rabbi Walters thinks this relates to the *Torah shebaal peh*: the *Torah shebichtav* is like *Zeir Anpin*, with the essential *mitzvos*. How to apply them, stricter or more lenient, requires understanding the people and their situation as they are.
So we renew on *Rosh Hashanah*, on *Rosh Chodesh* or every day: we want to be G-dly, but we re-commit in a new way based on who we are, which is always changing.

The command we receive, to be G-d's people, changes. *Rosh Hashanah* is the head of the year, which means change, and our ability to change comes from the *bittul* we express then. We recognize that we really want to do what G-d wants, and we re-evaluate the best way to express it.

We have to re-evaluate what G-d wants from us, and go all the way back to the beginning of the whole *seder hishtalshelus*, to the *Ein Sof* before *ana emloch*. The whole *seder* was made for the Jewish people.

The secret of the *Torah* is that its whole purpose is to help the Jewish people: *Yisroel*, the *Torah* and the Holy One are one. So understanding and expression are rebuilt for the needs of the people. The renewal goes back to the *hisnasus* in His essence, before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.en: and that's the whole reason that there was this original *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: כדי שיהיה דבר חוץ מן העצמות, שיתכן על זה בחינת אור ההתנשאות דבחינת מלכות דאין סוף
phrases.en: so that there should be something separate from His essence, so that there could be this expression of His transcendence

blocks.text: The first *tzimtzum*, called *makom panui*, made room for something outside His essence, where His transcendence, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, could be revealed. The whole process of creation came about for our *avoda*.

sections.title: Malchus of Atzilus comes down as the head of the foxes
sections.summary: The curtain between Atzilus and Beriya lets the Malchus of Atzilus come down, as a parent teaches a child, and this is why ani rishon and ani acharon are one.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין גמלתהו טוב
phrases.en: like it says elsewhere that G-d bestows good and not bad
about the reason that G-d creates idolaters

phrases.he: שהפרידן מאחדותו בבחינת החושך והצמצום כו',
phrases.en: G-d separated them from His unity and so they feel that they're separate
so that there could be this idea of *tiferes*

phrases.he: שמדת התפארת גם כן אינו אלא בפני איש נכרי ומרוחק דוקא

blocks.text: G-d bestows good and not bad. The root of the idolaters and of the *mazalos* is that He separated them from His unity, in darkness and *tzimtzum*, so they feel separate.

sensitivity.reason: Says G-d separated the idolaters from His unity. A Torah position about other religions, stated as such; the public text keeps the point and drops the group name.
sensitivity.publishable: G-d bestows good and not bad. The root of false beliefs and of the *mazalos* is that He separated them from His unity, in darkness and *tzimtzum*, so they feel separate.

blocks.text: The false beliefs themselves: why would G-d create a world with falsehood, where our intuition is often wrong and we make mistakes? Why is there the possibility of evil opposing His unity?

The darkness and *tzimtzum* create the feeling of separateness, which is the purpose of all the *tzimtzumim*, so that we can do *avoda*. Even evil is created intentionally for this purpose, so that *tiferes* can exist.

*Tiferes* is like showing off: you see real beauty only by contrast, by surpassing someone else. The example is a foreign, distant person. So G-d creates evil and falsehood so we can appreciate the beauty of the truth and of a G-dly life.
blocks.title: Showing off

phrases.en: and so too it's understood, coming all the way down to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*
which is the end of all levels of *Atzilus*

phrases.he: שהוא רצון ותענוג כו' של מדת ההתנשאות להיות מלך על בי"ע,
phrases.en: that this is the desire, this idea of transcendence and leadership to be the king over the separate creatures

phrases.he: שלזה הוצרך להיות הצמצום דמסך שבין אצילות לבריאה,
phrases.en: and this is what's motivating the *tzimtzum*
and become the head of the foxes

blocks.text: So too the *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, the end of all its levels, desires to be king over *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. That desire motivates the *tzimtzum* of the *masach* (curtain) between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, as the first *tzimtzum* was motivated by the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.
The curtain lets *Malchus* come down: in *Atzilus* it is the tail of the lion, and when it comes down it becomes the head of the foxes.
The immature view comes down as when you educate a child with candy and punishment. You come down to where the child is, because you can transcend yourself and want him to grow.
blocks.title: Candy for a child

blocks.text: Being mature and above that, you can come down to give them what they need, so you build a whole system suited to them. It projects something much lower than you, outside you, as is known.

phrases.he: והיינו אני ראשון בבחינת מלכות דאין סוף ואני אחרון במלכות דאצילות,
phrases.en: and this is what it says: *ani rishon* in the *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*, and *ani acharon* in the *Malchus* of *Atzilus*
because the beginning, the fact that G-d transcends all limits, is expressed in the end

phrases.he: וזהו בכל ראש השנה וראש השנה כידוע ודי למבין
phrases.en: and this is what's expressed in every *Rosh Hashanah*

blocks.text: *Ani rishon* is the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, *ani acharon* the *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. As the essential *middah* showed His transcendence, so He could be revealed even in *tzimtzum*, the power of limit.
*Malchus* of *Atzilus* creates creatures that feel separate, all the way down to the *kelipos*, to show that G-dliness can be found in everything, even in a person who feels low.
The beginning is rooted in the end: G-d's transcendence is expressed in His coming down even to the lowest things and being found everywhere. This is what is expressed each *Rosh Hashanah*.

*Malchus* is a deep, fundamental thing in the *Torah*, which is why we make a big deal of physical *mitzvos*. A *rav* worth his salt decides a *psak* in a similar way: when Moshe received the *Torah* there were forty-nine reasons to call a thing kosher and forty-nine to call it *posul*.
The *Torah* itself is objective, separate from what it means for a person. Bringing it out to a person is the idea of the *Torah shebaal peh*.

In *Kabbalah* we view things through the *hitlabshus* (clothing) of how they appear from a human perspective, since the purpose is to help people and reveal G-dliness in them. We want to understand the objective part, then plug it into people, and that ability comes from *Malchus*.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does Malchus in its essence express itself as hisnasus, and why is that higher than the other sefiros?
Why does hisnasus need something outside itself, and how does bittul relate to kingship?
Why does Malchus start as a point, and why can it be built only once there is something separate?
What is built on Rosh Hashanah, and what is the Keser of the Nukva?
How are the sefiros a projection from us, and why is Malchus G-d relating to our perspective?
What is the first tzimtzum for, and what do ani rishon and ani acharon mean?
